rows.title: SAM-consumer shares (liver model)
rows.detail: GNMT 43.7%, PEMT 27.4%, GAMT 25.3%, DNMT 2.0% (Reed 2015: 44 / 27 / 25 / 2); max deviation 0.2%

rows.title: SAM-consumer shares against the whole-body budget of parameters-b2
rows.why: The base calibration follows the Reed liver model (GNMT 44%). The B2 budget is whole-body and puts GNMT at ~15% (liver-only ~21%). Select the samConsumerBudget variant "b2budget" for the alternative; the glycine ensemble samples GNMT flux over 15-44 uM/h.
rows.detail: GNMT 43.7% (whole-body budget 14.5%, range 9.5-31%), creatine 25.3% (budget 36%, range 18-73%)

rows.title: Transmethylation / transsulfuration partition
rows.detail: transsulfuration 49.7% of homocysteine disposal; 2.01 methionine cycles per cystathionine (Mudd >= 1.9)

rows.title: BHMT share of remethylation
rows.detail: BHMT 48.9% of remethylation

rows.title: Methionine balance
rows.detail: methionine in 51.500 = CBS 50.000 + Hcy export 1.500 uM/h

rows.title: Absolute flux scale: liver share of whole-body transmethylation
rows.why: The Reed 2015 liver cycle (100 uM/h) is 2.4 mmol/day at 1 L, 12% of the whole-body 20 mmol/day. Whole-body loads are therefore converted with a proportional share (loadScale 5 uM/h per mmol/day, ensemble range 3-15), not at absolute scale. Documented scale inconsistency between B1 and B2.
rows.detail: model liver (1 L) transmethylation 101 umol/h = 2.4 mmol/day = 12.1% of whole-body 20 mmol/day

rows.title: Total folate pool
rows.why: The model tracks THF, CH2-THF, 5-MTHF, 10-formyl-THF (incl. methenyl) and DHF: 14.4 uM. Reed's 20 includes forms and bound pools that are not modelled. The sum is conserved; only ratios between forms matter for the effects.
rows.detail: 14.4 uM of modelled folate forms (Reed total 20)

rows.title: GNMT glycine saturation at hepatic glycine
rows.detail: GNMT glycine saturation 92.7% with Km 130 uM (B1 note: ~93%), 45.4% with Km 2 mM

rows.title: PEMT flux as fraction of the liver PC pool
rows.why: B2 holds two incompatible PEMT numbers: the SAM budget (3.75 mmol/day; Reed 27.5 uM/h SAM = 9.2 uM PC/h here) and the PC-pool fraction (0.53%/h x 17.3 mM = 92 uM PC/h, i.e. 275 uM/h of SAM). The model follows the SAM budget; the PC-pool number would exceed all other SAM consumers combined.
rows.detail: PEMT makes 0.053%/h of the PC pool (Pynn 2011: 0.53%/h, range 0.27-1.06)

rows.title: Plasma glycine after 4.6 g (1 mmol/kg lean mass)
rows.detail: peak 953 uM at 35 min (Gannon 2002, unverified secondhand: 217 -> 909 uM at 40 min; 414 uM at 120 min, model 512)

rows.title: Plasma betaine after 50 mg/kg
rows.detail: Cmax 961 uM at 0.88 h, late half-life 22.3 h (Schwahn 2003, 50 mg/kg: 939 uM, 0.9 h, 14.4 h [6-32])

rows.title: Betaine lowers fasting tHcy in a dose-dependent way
Betaine lowers the post-methionine-load tHcy increment
rows.detail: post-load tHcy increment 4.7 -> 3.8 uM with betaine 6 g/day (-20.2%; Olthof 2003: -40%)

rows.title: Choline lowers fasting tHcy
rows.detail: tHcy -11.8% at +2.6 g choline/day (Olthof 2005: -18%)

rows.title: Choline and betaine raise BHMT flux and lower hepatic Hcy
rows.detail: BHMT flux 36.8% (choline 2 g/day), 52.5% (betaine 3 g/day); liver Hcy -15.7% / -21.3%

rows.title: MTHFR 677TT-like (0.4x): tHcy up, 5-MTHF down
rows.detail: MTHFR 0.4x: tHcy 52.6%, 5-MTHF -45.6%, SAM:SAH -16.1%

rows.title: B6 restriction raises cystathionine
rows.detail: cystathionine 68.2% at PLP 41% (Gregory 2013: +52% and +66%)

rows.title: B6 restriction leaves fasting tHcy unchanged
rows.why: With cellular PLP at 41% (assumed equal to plasma PLP) CBS falls to 70% and Hcy must rise ~35% to restore flux (Km 1 mM, linear regime). Hepatic PLP probably falls less than plasma PLP; with PLP at 75% the model change is small. Ensemble range of kplp_cbs 0.3-0.6 does not cover the observed flat response.
rows.detail: fasting tHcy 24.3% (restriction study: unchanged)

rows.title: B6 restriction raises glycine
rows.why: SHMT and GCS are scaled by the same PLP factor (K 0.10), so glycine barely moves (+2%); in vivo the glycine rise compensates the lower enzyme activity (cleavage flux unchanged). Weak data (n.s. in the largest cohort).
rows.detail: hepatic glycine 2.4% (plasma glycine +10-29% in restriction studies)

rows.title: B6 restriction enlarges the post-load tHcy increment
rows.detail: post-load tHcy increment 4.7 -> 6.3 uM (B6 restriction: larger, Ubbink 1996)

rows.title: B12 deficiency: methyl-folate trap and hyperhomocysteinaemia
rows.detail: B12 0.2x: 5-MTHF 113.7%, THF -70.9%, 10-formyl-THF -62.5%, tHcy 87.3%, total folate 0.0%

rows.title: B12 deficiency lowers SAM:SAH
rows.why: The trapped 5-MTHF inhibits GNMT (Reed/Yeo mechanism), cutting SAM consumption and raising SAM:SAH. Parameter-dependent: with weak folate inhibition (Ki > ~100 uM) the sign flips (see ensemble). Not settled in humans.
rows.detail: SAM:SAH 28.6% (cobalamin-deficiency literature: SAM low-normal, SAH up; model: trapped 5-MTHF inhibits GNMT)

rows.title: Niacin load raises SAH and lowers SAM:SAH
rows.detail: niacin 2 g/day: SAH 21.9%, SAM -38.1%, SAM:SAH -49.2%, NNMT 52 uM/h

rows.title: Niacin raises tHcy
rows.why: tHcy rises by only a few percent at 1 g/day because the extra-hepatic half of plasma Hcy is unaffected by the hepatic methyl sink. Size, not sign, disagrees.
rows.detail: tHcy 3.7% at 1 g/day niacin (Garg 1999: +17% during titration to 1 g, +55% at 18 weeks)

rows.title: Fraction of niacin methylated by NNMT
rows.detail: 64.1% of niacin methylated at 2 g/day (B2: 4.38-6.3 mmol methyl/g of 8.12 mmol/g = 54-78%)

rows.title: Glycine bolus raises GNMT flux and sarcosine
rows.why: Only the Luka-style (mM) Km gives a transient GNMT rise; sarcosine is cleared by SARDH within an hour so its peak stays flat. With the Reed Km (130 uM, 93% saturated) GNMT flux falls slightly because SAM feedback (Hill 2) and 5-MTHF inhibition outweigh the glycine term. Hypothesis-level; no human data.
rows.detail: 10 g glycine bolus, peak GNMT flux / sarcosine / trough SAM:SAH: Reed Km 1.7% / 0.0% / -1.6%; Luka Km 9.5% / 3.8% / -9.0%

rows.title: Chronic glycine raises hepatic sarcosine
rows.why: Model sarcosine does not rise (SAM and GNMT feedback, rapid SARDH). Mouse, high-fat diet, 6 weeks - far outside the model regime; shown as an unreproduced observation.
rows.detail: chronic glycine 10 g/day: liver sarcosine -5.6% (Reed Km), -1.7% (Luka Km); mouse +86% (Alves 2022)

rows.title: Glycine supplementation and tHcy
rows.why: Extra glycine raises serine through SHMT (serine +17% in Tan 2025 too), which in the model enhances CBS and lowers Hcy; the human data show a small rise. Serine/CBS coupling and the SHMT exchange flux are unconstrained assumptions.
rows.detail: tHcy -8.9% at 7 g/day glycine (Tan 2025: +0.6 uM = +6%); the serine -> CBS arm lowers Hcy in the model

rows.title: Low folate supply: SAM down, tHcy up
rows.detail: folate supply 0.5x: total folate -50.0%, tHcy 46.1%, SAM -26.7%

rows.title: Methionine load test (100 mg/kg)
rows.detail: 100 mg/kg methionine: tHcy peaks 67.8% at 4.8 h after the dose (clinical test: roughly +100% at 4-8 h)

rows.title: GNMT loss raises SAM 30-fold
rows.why: SAM rises only x2.6 (x6.5 with GAMT Km 6.7 uM): other consumers (GAMT, PEMT) keep spare capacity and MAT-I is SAM-inhibited, so the calibrated network buffers SAM. In vivo methionine rises 7-25x as well, which the model (net methionine input fixed) cannot do. Direction right, magnitude not: GNMT-dependent SAM effects should be read as lower bounds.
rows.detail: GNMT activity 0: SAM x2.6 (human deficiency x28-47, mouse x36), SAH -18.0% (mouse: falls 12-15 -> 3-5)

rows.title: BHMT loss: SAM down, SAH and tHcy up
rows.why: SAM falls in the right direction but SAH falls and tHcy rises only 1.5x: CBS (linear in Hcy, Km 1 mM) absorbs the extra Hcy in the model, whereas the knockout mouse cannot. Net methionine input is fixed by construction.
rows.detail: BHMT activity 0: SAM x0.74 (mouse x0.57), SAH x0.87 (mouse x2.6), tHcy x1.47 (mouse x8)

rows.title: Total folate is conserved by the closed folate reactions
rows.detail: closed folate reactions conserve total folate; the only open reactions are fol_in, fol_loss_ch2thf, fol_loss_dhf, fol_loss_f10, fol_loss_mthf, fol_loss_thf

rows.title: Methyl-group accounting with boundary exchanges
rows.detail: internal methyl transfers (MAT, GNMT, PEMT, BHMT, MTR, MTHFR, DMGDH, SARDH, CHDH, Kennedy, PLD) conserve methyl groups; 26 boundary reactions exchange them: bet_efl, bet_up, cho_abs, cho_diet, cho_in, cho_out, dmg_out, d
